items.Title: What is Epic Haiku?
items.Answers: Epic Haiku is a mobile application designed for healthcare providers, allowing them to access the Epic electronic health record (EHR) system from their smartphones or tablets. It enables convenient access to patient information, messaging, and schedule management on the go.

items.Title: How do I download and install Epic Haiku?
items.Answers: Epic Haiku can be downloaded from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store. After installation, you'll need to configure the app with your organization's server settings, which can be obtained from your IT department.

items.Title: What can I do with Epic Haiku?
items.Answers:
With Epic Haiku, you can:

  • View patient charts, including lab results, medications, and medical history.
  • Manage your schedule and review upcoming appointments.
  • Communicate securely with other providers or care team members.
  • Capture clinical photos and securely upload them to the patient’s record.

items.Title: Is Epic Haiku secure?
items.Answers: Yes, Epic Haiku uses secure, encrypted connections to ensure that patient data is protected. It complies with HIPAA regulations to safeguard patient privacy.

items.Title: Can I use Epic Haiku to prescribe medications?
items.Answers: ​Epic Haiku allows you to view patient medications and make medication-related notes, but prescribing capabilities may vary depending on your organization's configuration. Check with your IT department for specific features available in your setup.

items.Title: What devices are compatible with Epic Haiku?
items.Answers: Epic Haiku is compatible with iOS and Android devices. Ensure that your device is running a supported version of the operating system as specified in the app's requirements on the App Store or Google Play.

items.Title: How do I troubleshoot issues with Epic Haiku?
items.Answers: If you encounter issues, first ensure that your app and device are updated to the latest versions. If problems persist, contact your IT support team for assistance with configuration or connectivity issues.

items.Title: How do I log in to Epic Haiku?
items.Answers: You can log in to Epic Haiku using your standard Epic credentials. Ensure that your device is connected to the internet and that you have the necessary server information configured in the app.

items.Title: Who should I contact for help with Epic Haiku?
items.Answers: For any issues or questions related to Epic Haiku, contact your organization's IT support team. They can assist with installation, configuration, and troubleshooting.

items.Title: Can I access Epic Haiku outside of my healthcare facility?
items.Answers: Yes, as long as you have an internet connection and the necessary security configurations in place, you can access Epic Haiku from anywhere.

items.Title: Why did we change from aXium and what is Epic?
items.Answers:
The change from aXium to Epic Wisdom was made to provide UT Dentistry with a more secure, integrated and efficient electronic health record system. Epic Wisdom offers a powerful and comprehensive platform that provides a full health history for patients with existing medical records in Epic through other care providers.


Epic is a leading provider of electronic health record solutions used by healthcare organizations to manage patient information, streamline workflows and improve outcomes. More information on Epic can be found on their website.

 

Epic Wisdom makes it easier for our users to combine a patient’s medical and dental history, including allergies, previous procedures, medications, and more, in one location. It also improves collaboration and communication between teams to facilitate secure and safe patient care management.

 

The transition to Epic aligns UT Dentistry’s electronic health record system with other UT Health San Antonio patient care groups. The update coincides with the opening of the new Multispecialty and Research Hospital, which will also use Epic.

items.Title: Can patients pay their bills electronically on Epic?
items.Answers: Patients can review previous bills and payments and see and pay any outstanding balances electronically on Epic through the patient portal (MyChart), allowing for convenient and secure payment options.

items.Title: Why is Thrive training important?
items.Answers:
According to the KLAS Arch Collaborative, clinicians who spend 3-5 hours a year on ongoing training are 2-3 times more satisfied with their EHR.1. 

Thrive training helps clinicians establish good efficiency habits and tailor their workspaces to support their personal workflows. Users can apply the knowledge from Thrive training to their own work or use it to help educate others. Thrive training is hands-on and moves at a pace that encourages questions and participation, allowing clinicians to walk away from class ready to use what they learned the next time they log in to the system for patient care.

items.Title: Who is the intended audience for Thrive training?
items.Answers:
Thrive classes are designed for clinicians who are using Epic in their day to day job. Thrive training is particularly impactful for clinicians who understand their core workflows but would like to increase their efficiency in the system. These users can be identified through self-selection or through efficiency data provided by tools like Signal, ASAP PEP, and NEAT.

Epic-led Thrive training is open to existing End-User Training Services (EUTS) organizations, as well as organizations who haven't yet used EUTS. If you are not already participating in EUTS, talk to your Epic representative to get started.

items.Title: Can more than one provider use Abridge to contribute to a note (e.g., resident + attending)?
items.Answers:
Unfortunately, no. Only one provider can record a note for a given encounter. However, an attending may record a resident’s patient presentation or readout. In the inpatient setting, multiple providers may create and record their own individual notes.

  • Option 2: Add Abridge dot phrases to your existing note templates using SmartPhrase Manager.

items.Title: Inpatient Insights
items.field_2:
Rounding clinicians see a complex mix of patients, ranging from those they've been checking in with every day to those they've never met before. To help them quickly prepare for each of those patients, they can use generative AI to create three types of insights to fit the type of information and level of detail that would be most helpful: 

- Patient Story insights are designed to familiarize clinicians with a patient they have not previously encountered. These summaries include history from notes and chart data, recent events, and other details related to the current admission, helping them prioritize and plan their care efficiently. Patient Story summaries are organized into three sections: history, events during admission, and recent events. The recent events section includes similar information to the freestanding Recent Events summary described below.

- Notes summaries focus on summarizing relevant details from recent notes on the patient, helping clinicians quickly get up to speed on recent observations and developments or see highlights from the rest of the treatment team. 

- Recent Events summaries provide an overview of recently documented information on the patient, including intake/output, medications, results, orders, the problem list, notes, vitals, nursing assessments, and code events, ensuring that clinicians are aware of significant recent changes in a patient's condition since the last time they rounded.

items.Title: PB Coding Assistant
items.field_2:
Save coders time so they can process more sessions and focus on those that require more expertise, helping maximize reimbursements. The Coding Assistant shows coders a list of potential diagnosis and procedure codes they might want to add based on notes that are relevant to a particular charge session, helping them review charge sessions efficiently and avoid jumping between many activities in search of relevant information.

Qualifying notes are automatically processed behind the scenes before a coder reviews the session, and they can jump to the source of supporting documentation when they need additional context. Cited text is highlighted in the note so they can decide whether the suggestion makes sense, all without needing to access Chart Review. When they decide to use a potential code, they can quickly add, swap, or remove codes from the charge session directly.

items.Title: InBasket Categorization
items.field_2: Is currently being piloted by specific departments. In Basket automatically categorizes patient-initiated messages into subjects like Clinical Advice, Paperwork, or Scheduling, using a predictive model to help care teams triage and prioritize incoming requests. This allows staff to filter messages based on their roles, reducing response times and improving efficiency in handling patient communications.

items.Title: InBasket Urgency
items.field_2: Is currently being piloted by specific departments. The Potentially Urgent predictive model automatically assigns urgency levels to patient messages, helping clinicians prioritize responses to potentially urgent communications while managing increasing message volumes. Currently, it categorizes messages as urgent, routine, or low (for FYI messages), with the option for users to manually select high urgency when needed.

items.Title: Outpatient Insights
items.field_2: Outpatient Insights leverages generative AI to create patient visit summaries 36 hours prior to appointments, allowing clinicians to save time on preparation and stay informed about past visits, including external notes from Care Everywhere. The system automatically updates summaries if there are changes to the patient's record and generates new ones for walk-in appointments. Clinicians can personalize their summaries by selecting specific notes or topics of focus and have access to citations for each point, enabling them to quickly reference relevant context.

items.Title: ART: Augmented Response Technology
items.field_2: Is currently being piloted by specific departments. Draft by Art streamlines communication for clinicians and staff by leveraging generative AI to create draft responses to patient messages. The system analyzes incoming messages from patients along with pertinent patient information to anticipate how a clinician or staff member might reply. It then generates a draft response that can be easily modified before being sent to the patient.

items.Title: Ambient Orders
items.field_2: Ambient AI tools utilize passive listening technology to capture clinical encounters through discreet devices, employing natural language processing and machine learning to structure, code, and stage draft orders directly in the clinician's EHR system. This automation enhances efficiency, boosts patient engagement, reduces clinician burnout, and improves accuracy by minimizing manual data entry errors.

items.Title: Abridge tab in Hypersapce
items.field_2: Clinicians can access Abridge features directly within the Epic Hyperspace interface, enabling them to summarize clinical documentation in brief sentences or short paragraphs. This integration aims to alleviate the documentation burden and reduce clinician burnout, allowing healthcare providers to concentrate more on patient care.

items.Title: Direct-to-patient MyChart recruitment
items.field_4: Use MyChart to find out whether potentially eligible patients are interested in participating in a study. The patient indicates whether she's interested in participating, and an In Basket message is sent to users at your organization.

items.Title: Front-End Accountability and Workqueue structure
items.field_4:
During our site visit, leaders in the revenue cycle breakout mentioned that they often spend extra time because pre-registration is not complete. 

We strongly recommend that front-end staff work front-end errors. We learned that, often times, managers don't enforce front end staff to correct pre-reg errors.

Responses to the Epic-released questions are stored in SmartData elements, which allows patients to see their previous answers if they modify their profile.

items.Title: Charge Capture Navigator​ (new)
items.field_4: As UT Health San Antonio moves towards an integrated healthcare delivery system, we are standardizing charging to ensure accurate revenue capture across our Epic system at the appropriate points in a patient's care. This eliminates the need to enter separate charge orders for each item or procedure, while keeping clinical orders—such as those for labs, imaging, medications, and procedures—focused on patient care and treatment tracking.

items.Title: Improve Cancer Staging Compliance
items.field_4:
The current rate of discrete cancer staging documentation is ~7% of all eligible cancer  problems are staged when a Beacon plan is applied. The vast majority of cancer staging is being documented as free text in notes.
cancer staging compliance by expanding security and adjusting workflows for tumor registrars and/or oncology support staff to take over as data entry for discrete staging data that is then routed to the provider to review and sign. Monitor and track compliance through the use of close encounter decision support to match your workflows. 
In the Foundation system we've built out a rule-based cancer staging BPA that warns clinicians upon interacting with the patient's chart or orders that they have a cancer diagnosis that does not have staging complete.

Additionally, soft stop reminders for encounter closure will enhance compliance with discrete staging, addressing the current challenge of free-text documentation in notes.

items.Title: Specialty Content Review – Neurology (RW4) (new)
items.field_4:
We are excited to announce several enhancements in Epic designed specifically for the Neurology Clinic. These improvements aim to streamline workflows and enhance patient care. Here’s what you can expect:
Refreshed Neurology-Specific Snapshot and Sidebar Reports: A more intuitive and organized view tailored to neurology needs, providing easier access to critical information.
New Pediatric Epilepsy Learning Health System (PELHS) SmartForm: A specialized SmartForm to support the management of pediatric epilepsy patients, enabling efficient documentation and tracking.
Seizure Action Plan: A dedicated feature to help clinicians quickly document and manage seizure action plans for patients.

Procedure Documentation: Improved tools for documenting neurology-specific procedures with precision and ease.
Neuro Exam SmartForm: A new form designed to simplify the documentation of neurological exams, ensuring comprehensive and standardized entry of clinical data.
Refreshed Navigator Layout: The navigator has been restructured to be more user-friendly and better aligned with clinical workflows in neurology.

items.Title: Cash Management
items.field_4: Cash Management allows cash reconciliation with the customer's bank to happen within Epic rather than being external.  With this functionality, individual checks within an 835 file are checked against a list of 'Cash Records' that correspond to specific deposits made by payers into the customer's account.  This way, we can ensure that payments are only posted in Epic after the money hits the account.

items.Title: Specialty Content Review – Urology (RW4) (new)
items.field_4:
We are excited to announce a set of enhancements in Epic designed specifically to improve your workflow and patient care experience in the Urology Clinic. These changes will go live soon and include:
Refreshed Urology-Specific Snapshot: The Urology Snapshot has been updated to display the most relevant patient information at a glance, making it easier to review key details during patient visits.
Updated Navigator Layout: The Navigator has been streamlined and optimized for Urology-specific needs, ensuring faster access to the tools and documentation fields you use most frequently.
New Urology Condition-Specific Synopsis Tools: dedicated Urology specific  Condition Synopsis tools have been added to provide a comprehensive overview of a patient's condition history, helping you make more informed clinical decisions quickly.

items.Title: Executive Dashboards
items.field_4: The web based executive dashboards allow users to summarize metrics via charts and graphs. The dashboards give the ability to view near real-time info and trending, incorporate Epic and non-Epic data as well as drill down into details.

items.Title: Lab Ordering and Collection Workflows
items.field_4: Implement the Resulting Agency field in the order composer for lab orders and consolidate the list of available order classes. Generate specimen collection tasks for lab-performed tests with specimens being collected in the clinics. Use ASP logic to default the resulting agency based on the patient's insurance or the department's preferred lab.

items.Title: Palliative Care Navigator
items.field_4:
The Palliative Care Navigator gives palliative care clinicians a central place to document the care they provide their patients so they can complete their common workflows without having to switch between different activities. The Palliative Care Tools Navigator includes navigator sections for:
- Reviewing the care the patient has received. This includes documentation from the current admission and past palliative care consults.
- Documenting the patient's episodes, a pain and symptom assessment, prognostic indicators, nutrition status, psychosocial assessment, spiritual assessment, fall risk, and skin risk.
- Educating the patient on their serious illness and documenting the conversation.
- Documenting the dates of palliative care conferences.

items.Title: Automated Claim Attachments

items.Title: Specialty Content Review – Cardiology (RW4) (new)

Cardiology Synopsis - Hypertension View: A dedicated view focused on hypertension-related patient data, designed to streamline access to key information.
Cardiology Heart Failure View: This view will help centralize and simplify monitoring and treatment documentation for heart failure patients.
New Cardiology SmartSet: A customizable SmartSet to assist with comprehensive and standardized treatment plans, making it easier to follow established protocols.
Hypertension HPI (History of Present Illness): This new section in the HPI will allow you to document hypertension specifics in greater detail, enhancing accuracy in patient records.
Cardiology Tab in Notewriter: A new dedicated tab in Notewriter will provide quicker access to cardiology-specific documentation tools, streamlining note-taking and improving documentation consistency.

items.Title: Hello World Billing Notifications
items.field_4:
For Hello World Billing's SMS notifications, it’s important to clarify the key information typically communicated to end users. Here’s a general overview:
Account Balance Information: SMS notifications can inform users about current balances, overdue amounts, or successful payments.
Due Date Reminders: Friendly reminders a few days before payment due dates to help users avoid late fees.
Payment Confirmation: Users receive confirmations for successful payments, providing assurance and record of the transaction.
Dispute Notifications: For any billing disputes or adjustments, an SMS may inform users of resolution statuses.
Support and Contact Information: SMS notifications often include details on how users can contact support for billing questions.
Opt-in/Opt-out Options: Users should have the ability to manage their SMS notifications preferences for billing information.

items.Title: Trusted Exchange Framework (TEFCA)
items.field_4: The Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement™, also known as TEFCA™, outlines a common set of principles, terms, and conditions to support the development of a Common Agreement that helps enable the nationwide exchange of electronic health information (EHI) across disparate health information networks (HINs). items.Title: Extract Sciences - Aura Integration
items.field_4:
Aura brings the promise of precision medicine within reach for the entire Epic community.  With Aura, you can collaborate with specialty diagnostic labs in a fraction of the time necessary to configure traditional interfaces. Connect to a single compendium of tests from each participating lab, then download purpose-built configuration packages to update your local Epic build. After that,  providers can use their existing Epic workflows to send orders to and receive discrete results from any lab on the network.
Today, oncology end users noted that Natera, Caris, and Gaurdant were the most common specialty diagnostic labs being used. The core workflows for these tests are managed outside of Epic with results scanned and separate processes to share with patients via MyChart.
